tasks.short: Evaluate and revise architecture curricula, content and instructional methods

steps.what: Evaluate curricula and course materials against learning evidence
Plan revisions to learning outcomes and instructional methods
Write revised curricula, course content and teaching-method descriptions

loop.purpose: Draft revisions from the teacher's selected changes
loop.input: Revision brief, current text and permitted source materials
loop.output: Tracked revision draft linked to brief items
loop.check: Teacher checks learning progression, architectural meaning and consistency against the brief and original materials
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported additions return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates preserve structure but cannot express the selected pedagogical changes

steps.what: Check revised curriculum coherence and finish the internal course documents

tasks.design: Keep evaluation and revision planning with the teacher in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop rewrites the selected sections, with tracked changes for the teacher to check and finish; it does not publish the curriculum.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting connected course sections takes time after the substantive changes are decided.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled drafting can follow a revision brief and retain links to the source text.
tasks.still_hard: The teacher must decide whether the curriculum develops sound architectural judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Teaching experience reveals a weak learning sequence that fluent wording can conceal.
tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting decisions; curriculum responsibility stays the same.

reach.task: Map learning progression across architecture modules
reach.learn: Outcome alignment and studio assessment design

evidence.claim: A bounded model can draft curriculum revisions from a teacher's brief; architectural quality and the labour estimate require local testing.

assumptions: Boundary includes evaluation, planning and the revised internal course documents; publication is not performed by this design.
The teacher produces the revision brief in s2, naming affected section, intended outcome, selected change and source version. Its full capture time is counted.
No structured evaluation score or prewritten recommendation is assumed. Missing source material or unclear intended changes cause manual drafting.
Test native tracked changes, reusable sections and templates first; use a loop only for substantive rewriting. Same-system saves have no separate saving or self-gate.
unknowns: Rules for using teaching materials with a model
research_questions: Does checked drafting preserve progression between studio exercises and technical content?

already_counted.description: Brief writing, draft correction and final coherence checking remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain source access and test drafting instructions on changed course formats.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R86, gross14 minus4 upkeep gives net10. Range2-7 assumes repeated text revisions; novel curriculum design retains all planning time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare architecture syllabi, assignments and handouts

steps.what: Gather source materials and course details for syllabi and assignments
Specify assignment aims, constraints and expected student outputs
Draft syllabi, homework assignments and handout explanations

loop.purpose: Draft explanations and assignment text from selected sources
loop.input: Material specification and permitted teaching sources
loop.output: Editable material text with source links
loop.check: Teacher checks factual claims, student workload, ambiguity and whether the exercise teaches the intended design skill
loop.stop: One correction pass, then manual completion for unsupported or confusing passages
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot write the course-specific explanations

steps.what: Lay out the syllabus, assignment sheets and handouts
Check course materials for accuracy, accessibility and complete instructions

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} templates for course structure and formatting, with a bounded loop for course-specific prose. The teacher specifies the exercise, corrects the text and checks the finished materials; no learner distribution is automated here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reusable course details still leave prose and page formatting to repeat.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document styles handle layout, while checked drafting helps express the teacher's brief.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible assignment can be too vague or require resources students cannot access.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher judges the learning value and feasibility of the exercise.
tasks.altitude: More preparation time can go to selecting useful architectural examples.

reach.task: Check assignment instructions against likely student questions
reach.learn: Accessible instructions and realistic studio workloads

evidence.claim: Native document templates can standardize layout and bounded models can draft teaching prose from supplied material; the combined time estimate is unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is preparation of finished materials, including syllabus and handout writing; publication and lecture delivery are separate activities.
Teacher-produced s2 specifies title, learning outcome, exercise constraints, expected deliverable, deadline and selected sources. Capture is counted in s2, not supplied for free.

The layout producer is the native template using s3's text and the existing course template; no model-generated date or reading is trusted. Missing template fields return to manual layout and checking.
Test native styles, section reuse and accessible templates before custom code. Formatting saves labour only where formatting is currently manual; file saving itself earns no saving.
unknowns: How much layout is already templated
Permission to process selected texts and images
research_questions: How long does a teacher need to correct generated assignments before students can understand them?

already_counted.description: Material specification, draft correction and final checks remain in retained time.

incremental.description: Maintain accessible templates, permitted sources and drafting examples.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R65, gross35 minus7 upkeep gives net28. Range10-20 assumes recurrent syllabus and handout structures with genuine manual layout; original studio design remains human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select architectural examples and sources for lectures
Prepare lecture structure and sequence examples
Write lecture explanations and speaker notes

loop.purpose: Draft explanations for the selected lecture sequence
loop.input: Teacher's lecture outline and selected architectural sources
loop.check: Teacher verifies technical meaning, visual references and suitability for the students' level
loop.stop: One correction pass then manual explanation of unclear technical claims
loop.why_not_simpler: Reusable outlines cannot express the particular architectural argument

steps.what: Check lecture notes and select the version to deliver
Deliver lectures and respond to students' questions

tasks.design: Use a reusable lecture structure in {DOCS} and bounded drafting for notes based on the teacher's selected sources. The teacher checks the prepared version and delivers the lecture, adapting explanations and answers live.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing an explanation from an established outline still consumes preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable outlines and checked drafting can assist the written preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Architecture lectures rely on visual reasoning and responsive explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher reads confusion and changes the explanation during the lecture.
tasks.altitude: Small preparation gains; teaching and responsibility for explanations stay human.

reach.task: Explain structural principles using architectural examples

evidence.claim: Checked model drafting can help prepare speaker notes; no saving in live teaching is assumed.

assumptions: This task owns lecture-specific outlines and speaker notes. Reusable syllabi and handouts belong to the separate materials task and are not counted again here.

The teacher produces the outline and selected source references in s1 and s2; their capture and checking are counted. Sources include title, location, selected example and relevant claim; missing sources mean manual writing.
Native outline reuse is tested before custom code. Structure time falls only for reused sections; the new argument and examples still require the teacher.
The delivery gate concerns the selected prepared notes and audience, not approval of an internal save. Live questions remain under the teacher's judgement.
unknowns: Share of preparation that is reusable
Amount of new architectural explanation required each lecture
research_questions: Does note assistance preserve the meaning of visual examples after teacher checking?

already_counted.description: Note correction and selecting the delivery version remain counted.

incremental.description: Keep lecture templates and permitted source collections usable.

approvals.approved_version: Prepared lecture-note version and intended student audience checked in s4; a changed prepared version requires a new check before delivery.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R91, gross9 minus3 upkeep gives net6. Range0-3 assumes recurrent lecture structures and checked notes; live delivery and answers retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate and grade architecture students' work, including design studios

steps.what: Retrieve students' work and the applicable assessment criteria
Evaluate architectural work against design and technical criteria
Discuss students' design reasoning and explain the studio critique
Record assessment observations and student-specific feedback points
Write and check feedback explaining the assessment of student work

loop.purpose: Express instructor observations as clear written feedback
loop.input: Instructor notes and assessment criteria without permission to change scores
loop.output: Draft feedback tied to instructor observations
loop.check: Teacher verifies every criticism and recommendation against the actual work and intended assessment
loop.stop: One correction pass then manual writing if a claim lacks an instructor observation
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed comment bank cannot fully express individual studio feedback

steps.what: Determine and record the student's grade
Release the final grade and checked feedback to the student

tasks.design: Configure the {LMS} assessment view to reduce retrieval, and use a bounded feedback draft from instructor notes in {DOCS}. Studio evaluation, critique, note capture and the grade stay with the teacher; release is a separate checked action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing useful individual feedback takes time beyond the studio critique and grading decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from instructor notes can help express an assessment without delegating the assessment itself.
tasks.still_hard: Architectural quality and design reasoning cannot be inferred safely from polished feedback text.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher examines drawings and models and understands the student's design choices.
tasks.altitude: A modest reduction in retrieval and feedback prose; grade authority does not change.

reach.role: art, drama, and music teacher, postsecondary
reach.task: Give evidence-based critique of creative student work
reach.learn: Specific formative feedback without replacing artistic judgement

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes; this supports feedback drafting, not architectural grading or this savings estimate.
The proposed architecture workflow and labour estimate are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes retrieval, physical studio evaluation, critique, written notes, feedback, grade recording and release. None is hidden inside the studio conversation.

The teacher produces student id, work version, criterion, observed feature and feedback point in s4, after evaluation and conversation. All capture time is retained. No automatic transcription or free structured rubric score is assumed.
The model drafts from those notes only. Missing observations return to manual feedback; no model-generated grade or unsupported judgement enters the record.

Native assessment views and comment banks are tested first. Their effect on note capture is assumed zero here. Internal saves earn no saving and no self-gate; the release gate binds the actual final student record.
unknowns: Whether current feedback tools already draft from notes
research_questions: Can checked feedback drafting preserve the teacher's exact assessment without adding claims about unseen work?

already_counted.description: Instructor note capture, feedback correction, grade decision and final release checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain allowed feedback prompts and inspect samples for unsupported criticism.

approvals.approved_version: Exact student id, submission version, grade and feedback text shown at release in s7; any change voids that check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R91, gross9 minus3 upkeep gives net6. Range0-3 assumes note-based feedback prose benefits; studio evaluation, conversation, grading and release retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Teachers retain curriculum, studio and grading decisions while reducing selected writing and formatting work.
reach: Coordinate learning progression with instructional coordinators
Share critique methods with creative-subject teachers
skills_to_grow: Separate assessment observations from feedback prose
role.ambitious_version: An architecture teacher with more preparation time for examples and studio learning, and unchanged responsibility for educational judgements.
